title: On Obeying the rule without question
subtitle: 品格修养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）
meta: 主题语境：品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）　|　核心词汇：obey　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 obey 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the musician ① obeyed the rule without question twice over, and every listener in the hall said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the musician ② obeys the rule without question year after year without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ obey the rule without question at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ obeyed the rule without question before — a line in the programme for December 1943 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Obeying the rule without question twice over, the musician said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ obey the customs of the house year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Obey the customs of the house at once and never mention it again.

By 1956 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the programme, and a new listener from the next hall ⑧ obeys the customs of the house twice over every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the piano, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ obeyed the rule without question again when nobody else would.

⑩ To obey the rule without question, my mother said in 1961, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the hall remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the hall forgets, somebody obeys the rule without question year after year again and somebody must obey the rule without question twice over all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 服从（一般过去式 obeyed the rule without question：1949 年乐师头一回这样做，来回两遍）
B. v. 服从（一般现在 obeys the rule without question：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 服从（不定式 to obey the rule without question：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 服从（过去完成时 had obeyed the rule without question：1943 年十二月的节目单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 服从（动名词 obeying the rule without question 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 遵守（obey the customs of the house：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去遵守遵守这户人家的惯例）
G. v. 遵守（obey the customs of the house：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 服从（后段两处：新来的听客照例 obeys the customs of the house，而母亲又一次 obeyed the rule without question）

answers.why: obey 意为“服从”，1949 年乐师来回两遍服从毫不迟疑地服从那条规矩，那是音乐厅里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 obeyed。
obey 意为“服从”，自那以后乐师年年地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 obeys。
obey 意为“服从”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯服从毫不迟疑地服从那条规矩”，此处为不定式 to obey the rule without question。
obey 意为“服从”，节目单里 十二月 那行字说明早在 1956 年之前就有人服从过，故用过去完成时 had obeyed。
obey 意为“服从”，乐师说“服从毫不迟疑地服从那条规矩这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 obeying the rule without question 作主语。
obey 意为“遵守”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去遵守遵守这户人家的惯例”，should ever 之后用原形 obey the customs of the house。
obey 意为“遵守”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻遵守遵守这户人家的惯例（obey the customs of the house at once），以后再也不要提起。
obey 意为“服从”，新来的听客每个夜晚都照例遵守遵守这户人家的惯例，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 obeys。
obey 意为“服从”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次来回两遍服从毫不迟疑地服从那条规矩，用一般过去式 obeyed 叙述。
obey 意为“服从”，结尾那句是母亲 1961 年的话：要服从毫不迟疑地服从那条规矩，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和音乐厅记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 obey 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the musician obeyed the rule without question twice over, and nobody in the hall forgot it.
Even now the musician obeys the rule without question year after year whenever the hall asks.
Obeying the rule without question twice over, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever obey the customs of the house year after year, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next hall obeys the customs of the house twice over every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother obeyed the rule without question again, and the hall remembered that half.
